To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Holstein calves from d 4-56 of life grew best when fed 19.6% crude protein (CP) starter.
calf starters with 19.6% crude protein, DM basis, support maximum growth of Holstein heifers.

Holstein calves fed calf starters containing 19.6% protein, DM basis, gained the most from weaning to 56 d of age, and calf growth was moderate when lower protein calf starters (15 or 18% crude protein) were fed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of different levels of protein in calf starters on calf growth.
the effects of calf starter protein level and calf starter intake on the performance of Holstein calves from d 4 of age through weaning.
the use of lower CP calf starters and the effect on performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calf starters containing 16.8 to 19.6% protein, DM basis, support calf growth as well as or better than those containing 22.4 or 15% protein, DM.
calf starters containing 19.6% crude protein (DM basis) support maximum growth of Holstein dairy calves from birth to 56 d of life.
the optimum protein content of a calf starter for calves from birth to weaning is 20% CP, DM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calf starters with 19.6% protein are recommended for Holstein calves.
calf starter CP contents of 19.6% (DM basis) or greater are recommended for Holstein calves from 1 to 56 d of life.
calves should be fed a calf starter with a minimum of 16.8% CP to maximize growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current NRC recommendation for calf starters (20% CP) is appropriate for Holstein calves.
calf starter diets should be formulated at a protein content that will support calf growth.
calves can grow well on calf starters containing 19.6% crude protein.
